title: Immutable audit provenance is treated as a current V-line product label
observed_behavior: The canonical active-document reference check exits 1 with DOC005 because the immutable baseline records the exact historical Git remote whose repository name ends in _V6.
expected_invariant: The active-document gate must stay green while exact historical provenance remains truthful; immutable evidence containing a versioned external identifier must either be classified as historical evidence or narrowly exempted from current product-label rules.
root_cause: The comprehensive-audit evidence pack remains under the active reviews tree and is not covered by the checker’s historical/version-label exclusions, so a literal provenance value is interpreted as current branding guidance.
failure_scenario: Every documentation validation run fails until a maintainer either falsifies the captured remote, weakens the rule broadly, or discovers the missing evidence classification manually.
evidence: Bundled-Python check_active_doc_references exited 1 and reported exactly DOC005 at BASELINE.md:15.
Line 15 is the backticked exact remote captured by the 2026-07-19 baseline, not an instruction to use a V-line release label.
The same document states that it is timestamped baseline/provenance evidence and distinguishes its historical HEAD from later snapshots.
existing_safeguards: DOC005 detects active V-line labels deterministically.
The checker already has explicit exclusions for historical/version-label contexts.
safeguard_gap: The active comprehensive-audit evidence location is not classified consistently with the immutable facts it is required to preserve.
tests_present: tests/python/tooling/test_active_doc_references.py covers DOC005 positive detection and known historical exclusions.
tests_missing: A fixture proving that a preserved audit baseline may retain an exact versioned remote without making the active-doc gate red.
recommended_remediation: Classify or archive this immutable evidence pack through the canonical documentation map, or add the narrowest path/context exclusion that preserves the literal remote while continuing to reject V-line labels in active guidance.
remediation_risk: Low; an overly broad exclusion could hide real branding drift, so keep any exemption path-specific and test it.
validation_rung: Run check_active_doc_references and its focused unit tests plus active-document link/reference checks; representative media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Exact-current reconciliation of the previously logged but unowned AUDIT-ERR-W12-ARCHIVE-007 event.

title: Launch and Settings review links resolve one directory below repository root
observed_behavior: All 44 repository-source links in the Launch review and all 90 in the Settings review use ../../ from docs/reviews/full-code-sweep-2026-07-09, resolving under docs/apps, docs/src, docs/ops, docs/tests, or docs/docs instead of the repository-root targets.
expected_invariant: Active review evidence must navigate to the cited current repository path so readers can verify each claim without manually repairing URLs.
root_cause: The two reviews computed repository-root-relative links from a directory that is three levels below root but used only two parent segments.
failure_scenario: A maintainer follows any of 134 evidence links and receives a missing target, preventing direct verification and making the active review look more authoritative than its navigable evidence supports.
evidence: A fenced-code-aware scan checked 1,500 local links across all 156 exact-current W12 active docs and found exactly 134 missing targets, all in these two files.
Adding one parent segment to each failed target resolves all 134 to existing repository files.
The same scan found zero missing Markdown anchors and zero unbalanced fences.
existing_safeguards: The linked labels retain source filenames and line ranges, making intended targets recoverable.
Git preserves the dated review text.
safeguard_gap: The canonical active-doc checker detects named legacy references and labels but does not validate relative Markdown targets.
tests_present: check_active_doc_references covers policy patterns, not general link resolution.
tests_missing: Repository-root-aware Markdown link validation for every active documentation path.
recommended_remediation: Change the affected repository-source targets from ../../ to ../../../, retain the already-correct docs-local links, then rerun a fenced-code-aware file/anchor/line-reference scan.
remediation_risk: Low; this is documentation-only, but review the diff to avoid changing intentionally docs-relative links.
validation_rung: Active-document link/reference check plus check_active_doc_references; representative media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current documentation defect; no current path-local finding covered these two reviews.

title: Four active code-sweep reviews retain 61 source line references beyond end of file

locations.symbol: 12 references beyond EOF after correcting the path prefix

observed_behavior: The dated Completed, Rename, and Schedule reviews contain 49 existing-file links whose cited final line is greater than the current target’s physical line count. Twelve more Settings citations are beyond EOF after applying the independently verified one-directory path correction, for 61 stale line references in total.
expected_invariant: An active review that cites exact source lines must either bind to an immutable source revision or keep every current-source line reference within the current target and update it after refactors.
root_cause: Large source modules were split or reduced after the 2026-07-09 reviews, while the review pack remained active and its current-file line anchors were not regenerated, archived, or commit-pinned.
failure_scenario: A reader opens a cited current file and cannot reach the claimed implementation; in several cases the current file is now a tiny compatibility/export surface, so the cited behavior moved elsewhere and the active review’s trace is materially ambiguous.
evidence: Exact line-count validation found 12 beyond-EOF references in completed-output-review.md, 28 in rename-review.md, and 9 in schedule-review.md.
After resolving all 90 Settings links with the verified parent-prefix correction, 12 cite settingsView.js or settingsWizard.js beyond their current 884/952 lines.

Representative drift includes completed/policy.py cited at lines 475, 542, 1427, and 1461 while the current file has 7 physical lines; renameView.js is cited as high as line 3440 while current length is 998.
existing_safeguards: The reviews are date-stamped and retain human-readable symbols/context.
Current source and generated summaries can be searched independently.
safeguard_gap: The active documentation system has no revision-pinned citation format or validator for source line ranges.
tests_missing: An active-doc reference test that validates source line suffixes and requires dated snapshot reviews to be commit-pinned or archived when their anchors drift.
recommended_remediation: Either archive/pin these reviews to their audited commit and label them historical, or update each citation to the current owner/symbol and rerun exact file/line validation. Do not merely clamp invalid numbers to EOF.
remediation_risk: Low to medium for documentation: mechanically changing numbers can misattribute behavior after module splits, so semantic owner lookup is required.
validation_rung: Exact local path and line-range scan plus current owner/symbol lookup for every changed citation; representative media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current traceability finding for active dated reviews; distinct from the relative-path construction defect.

title: Bundle overview still assigns Pending Publish to the Maintenance view
observed_behavior: The bundle overview says Maintenance has two tools and describes Pending Publish plus Publish Parked as its second tool. The current shell includes a dedicated Pending Publish page, and Publish Parked is a Launch mode; the Maintenance partial/assets contain neither label.
expected_invariant: The active bundle overview must map operator workflows to their current owning pages and must not direct mutation-capable recovery actions to a page that no longer exposes them.
root_cause: The overview predates the Pending Publish page split and Launch workflow placement, and was not updated when navigation ownership changed.
failure_scenario: An operator opens Maintenance expecting parked-output evidence or the drain action, cannot find it, and may conclude the bundled UI lacks the supported recovery workflow.
evidence: docs/README_MediaPipelineRemuxEncodeAIO.md lines 97-100 explicitly list Release Package and Pending Publish as two Maintenance tools.
Current app-shell navigation and page-pending.html expose a dedicated Pending Publish page.
page-launch.html exposes option value drain_pending_pushes with label Publish Parked; bounded searches found no Pending Publish or Publish Parked text in page-maintenance.html or maintenanceView.js.
existing_safeguards: The current WebView navigation visibly exposes Pending Publish.
Current project-state documentation separately identifies Pending Publish as its own workflow.
safeguard_gap: The older active overview remains a plausible entry point and has no generated ownership check against shell navigation.
tests_present: WebView route/navigation inventories cover current page ownership.
tests_missing: A documentation assertion tying workflow ownership statements in the bundle overview to the current navigation/page inventory.
recommended_remediation: Rewrite the Maintenance section to describe only current Maintenance functions, add a separate Pending Publish section, and locate Publish Parked under Launch while retaining backend-ownership and confirmation language.
remediation_risk: Low; documentation-only, but preserve the distinction between read-only pending evidence and the backend-owned drain command.
validation_rung: Active-doc checks plus WebView navigation/touchpoint inventory checks; representative media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current active-document ownership drift; no current finding referenced this overview path.

title: Nine active-document summaries and PROJECT_INDEX records fingerprint older source bytes
observed_behavior: For each listed active document, its generated summary frontmatter and PROJECT_INDEX source_hash agree with one another but disagree with the exact current source SHA-256. The canonical refresh_summaries --check reports four tooling/test summaries and omits all nine active-document mismatches.
expected_invariant: Summary-first navigation and PROJECT_INDEX lookup must identify the exact current bytes of every summarized active document, and the canonical full check must enumerate every tracked summary class.
root_cause: These active documents changed after their summary/index generation, while the full freshness checker’s census does not compare this active-document summary class; concurrent documentation generation is not atomic with source and index updates.
failure_scenario: An agent follows the required summary-first workflow and scopes work from stale purpose, authority, relationships, or hashes even after the canonical four reported summary failures are repaired.
evidence: Fresh build_rows comparison found exactly nine W12 active docs with project_index_present=true and project_index_hash_matches=false.
Each expected docs/generated/summaries/<source>.md artifact exists and declares the same older source hash as PROJECT_INDEX.
refresh_summaries --check exited 1 naming four different tooling/test summaries and none of these nine active docs.
existing_safeguards: Summary frontmatter and PROJECT_INDEX both retain exact source hashes.
build_rows independently compares current source bytes with PROJECT_INDEX.
safeguard_gap: The canonical all-summary check omits these tracked active-doc summaries, and current generation is not bound to a settled writer epoch.
tests_missing: A tracked-summary census proving every docs/generated/summaries artifact is paired with its declared source and PROJECT_INDEX in one settled snapshot.
recommended_remediation: After documentation writers quiesce, regenerate these nine summaries and PROJECT_INDEX together, then extend the full checker to enumerate active-document summaries and assert exact source/summary/index joins.
remediation_risk: Low for deterministic generated text; running before writer freeze can immediately recreate the mismatch.
validation_rung: Full summary freshness check, exact nine source/summary/index hash joins, summary-integrity tests, and fresh build_rows inventory; representative media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: Exact-current recurrence and expansion of W12-010, which recorded five of these document-summary pairs as transiently resolved in an earlier snapshot; the current HEAD now has nine stale pairs.
